before.name: Peter Niven Kiger
before.description: Peter Niven Kiger was a Quaker pacifist and Committee for Nonviolent Action and War Resisters League organizer. He served about one year in federal prison beginning in 1961 after refusing civilian alternative service as a conscientious objector. On March 24, 1966, he burned his draft card at a New York press conference protesting conscription and the Vietnam War. He was convicted in 1969 and served a three-month federal prison sentence. Exact admission and release dates for both imprisonments remain unresolved.
